messages.subject: Allele specific estimates from AvgCnPlm
parts:
Hi Henrik,

I am trying to get allele-specific raw intensity estimates from for
Affy 6.0 chips, by doing:

AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=FALSE, shift=+300)

But somehow it's not working. Below is my entire script:

###

library(aroma.affymetrix)
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6", tags="Full")
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("Spellman44TrainingSamples", cdf=cdf)
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=FALSE, shift=
+300)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
gi <- getGenomeInformation(cdf)
units <- getUnitsOnChromosome(gi,chromosome=22)
pos <- getPositions(gi,units=units)
unitNames <- getUnitNames(cdf,units=units)
theta <- extractMatrix(ces,units=units)

###

The command "print(ces)" confirms that combine Alleles was set to
FALSE:

> print(ces)
CnChipEffectSet:
Name: Spellman44TrainingSamples
Tags: ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300
Path: plmData/Spellman44TrainingSamples,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300/
GenomeWideSNP_6
Platform: Affymetrix
Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_6,Full,monocell
Number of arrays: 44
Names: A1, A10, ..., D9
Time period: 2008-06-10 02:32:06 -- 2008-06-10 02:32:10
Total file size: 1185.77MB
RAM: 0.04MB
Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm", mergeStrands: logi TRUE,
combineAlleles: logi FALSE)

If it gives allele-specific intensities, then the matrix should have
2*(number of samples) columns. I had 44 samples, but the resulting
theta matrix contains only 44 columns:

> dim(theta)
[1] 36572 44

A call to sessionInfo() gave the following:

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.6.2 Patched (2008-04-03 r45371)
i386-pc-mingw32

locale:
LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252;LC_CTYPE=English_United States.
1252;LC_MONETARY=English_United States.
1252;LC_NUMERIC=C;LC_TIME=English_United States.1252

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods
base

other attached packages:
[1] aroma.affymetrix_0.9.3 aroma.apd_0.1.3
R.huge_0.1.5
[4] affxparser_1.10.2 aroma.core_0.9.3
sfit_0.1.5
[7] aroma.light_1.8.1 digest_0.3.1
matrixStats_0.1.2
[10] R.rsp_0.3.4 R.cache_0.1.7
R.utils_1.0.2
[13] R.oo_1.4.3 R.methodsS3_1.0.1


What am I doing wrong? Thanks in advance for help!

Nancy

>> dim(theta)
> [1] 36572 44

Your assumption (that the allele signals are returned as paired
columns) was wrong. There are in total 24,513 units on chromosome 22;

> str(units)
int [1:24513] 34464 34465 34466 34467 34468 34469 34470 34471 34472 34473

Out of these 12,059 are SNP units and 12,454 are CN units:

> length(grep("CN_", unitNames))
[1] 12454
> length(grep("SNP_", unitNames))
[1] 12059

...and 2*12059+12454=36572 rows. Thus, the allele-specific estimates
are stored along the rows not the columns. You see this better if you
use extractDataFrame(), e.g.

> data <- extractDataFrame(ces, units=units, addNames=TRUE);
> data[1:10,]
unitName groupName unit group cell NA06985 ...
1 SNP_A-1970657 C 34464 1 68306 1235.4 ...
2 SNP_A-1970657 T 34464 2 68307 3232.4 ...
3 ...

So, group==1 indiciates allele A and group==2 indicates allele B. The
groupName indicates the allele nucleotide. For all CN units there are
only one group.

For your convenience, I've added an extractTheta() to the latest
version of aroma.affymetrix. That returns an 3-dimensional array,
where the 1st index is the unit, the 2nd the allele, and the last the
array, e.g.

> theta <- extractTheta(ces, units=units[c(1:10,24504:24513)]);

Thus, for the SNPs theta[,1,] and theta[,2,] holds the allele A and
allele B estimate, respectively. For the CN probes, theta[,1,] holds
the "total" theta and theta[,2,] is always NA.

Hope this helps

Henrik
